Aggregate Liquidation Map MODELED ESTIMATE

Refreshed 9/27/26, 1:56 AM
Where leveraged positions would be force-liquidated, by price & leverage tier — modeled from trading activity over the time window shown in each map's stats. Bars left of the price line = long liquidations (falling price), right = short (rising). The white curve is cumulative liquidation volume (right axis) — the running total wiped out if price sweeps from here to that level. Hover any price for the breakdown. The cyan price line and header price update live (WebSocket); the bars/walls are a snapshot from the last model build.

Real liquidations sit ~0.8% from price on average vs the model's ~5.6% resting walls — destruction clusters nearer because shallow sweeps are constant and deep ones rare. Weighting the walls by how often price actually reaches each level lifts alignment to 60% (raw 52%) — the model's wall placement is moderate. But they see only 53% of open interest (most sits on hyperliquid — 16% — which has no hourly OI feed), so this validates just that slice.
Indirect proxy: OI also drops on voluntary closes; side inferred from price direction; only venues publishing hourly OI contribute. Not a real-liquidation feed (that needs an always-on WebSocket collector).

⚠ read direction, not magnitude: 30-min snapshots with a 24h horizon overlap heavily, so the effective sample is far smaller than n. snapshots per token: BTC 2824 · NMR 2823 · ZEC 2823 · HYPE 2823 · SPACEX 2823 · MSTR 2823 · scored window 2026-07-16 → 2026-09-25 (only snapshots covered by archived klines count) · the matched base rate controls for distance, not for regime — confidence accrues with calendar time.
Method: distribution shape from per-candle open-interest growth (OI-Δ) where the venue provides OI history, else traded volume, across enabled venues over the displayed time window; total magnitude anchored to current open interest. Leverage tiers applied via liq ≈ entry·(1 ∓ 1/L) (linear USDT perps); entries whose liq level was already swept by the later price path (wicks included) are dropped, their share re-rested on surviving entries. This is a relative-intensity model, not real positions — no exchange publishes per-trader leverage (same category as Coinglass / Kingfisher). Built by fetch.mjs + render.mjs.
